one_line: Private semantic campaign codex for tabletop play.
what_it_does: Chronicles campaign facts and recalls NPCs, promises, and plot threads by meaning inside the browser tab.
leverage_rationale: Structured semantic writes and retrieval make a shared, inspectable campaign memory substantially more reliable than an agent searching notes or chat through the UI.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and description specify in-tab embeddings and vector search.
Human and agent share the editable codex state.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent focused codex and the frame sheets show a functioning-looking product surface, though end-to-end recall is not legible in the frames.
execution_evidence: Three product-motion frame sheets show the codex UI across states.
Description details recording, editing, and semantic recall workflows.
impact_rationale: Long-running tabletop campaigns and fiction projects have a concrete continuity and recall problem, and private semantic memory directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Description gives a specific ferryman/plot-thread recall use case.
Local/private architecture fits campaign secrets.
creativity_rationale: A local-first living world chronicle with agent-human co-maintenance is a fresh, memorable application of semantic memory.
creativity_evidence: Campaign codex framing and meaning-based recall are pursued as the core interaction.
usability_note: Inspectable shared codex and in-tab privacy support trust; tabletop setup and embedding latency may add friction.
red_flags: No transcript and fine-grained recall result is not legible in the frame evidence.
standouts: Private semantic recall for campaign continuity.
advance_reason: Strong differentiated use case and meaningful WebMCP/shared-state delta.

one_line: An agent that resolves contradictory delivery policies by seeking justified human discretion.
what_it_does: Runs a misdelivery scenario through explicit policy checks, evidence gathering, waiting, and escalation rather than inventing a loophole.
leverage_rationale: The product's value is a constrained, auditable agent action loop where tools encode policy boundaries and escalation; generic UI driving would be materially less safe and repeatable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch emphasizes minimum necessary agency and evidence-gated action.
Split-screen design compares human support friction with a five-tool agent workflow.
execution_rationale: The central scenario is sharply scoped and the packet describes a complete decision/escalation narrative; video evidence supports the product presentation.
execution_evidence: Two frame sheets show the product scenario across states.
Description specifies conflicting rules, evidence, waiting, and escalation behavior.
impact_rationale: Contradictory support policies are a real consumer problem, and refusing unsafe autonomy while still progressing is credible value.
impact_evidence: Concrete fresh-food misdelivery scenario.
Addresses both harmful invention and useless stalling.
creativity_rationale: Designing around knowing when not to act, with minimum necessary agency, is an unusually strong interaction concept for an agent product.
creativity_evidence: Core premise reverses the usual act-first agent framing.
Human escalation is part of the designed workflow.
usability_note: The policy-aware flow is legible, but real support integrations and human handoff could be operationally complex.
red_flags: No public repository and no transcript.
standouts: Excellent safety/agency thesis demonstrated through a relatable case.
advance_reason: Exceptional concept and WebMCP leverage with a concrete demonstrated scenario.

one_line: Agent-collaborative academic planning workspace for Stanford students.
what_it_does: Combines goals, course research, schedules, clubs, milestones, scratchpad notes, and activity history in one planning workspace.
leverage_rationale: Structured course and schedule state lets an agent plan precisely and maintain continuity across academic tasks where browser automation is brittle.
leverage_evidence: Description covers course catalog/sections, calendar, goals, and agent-authored changes.
Activity log distinguishes human and agent edits.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a broad but coherent workspace with many integrated surfaces, and three frame sheets show product states.
execution_evidence: Eight gallery images plus three video sheets are supplied.
Description enumerates landing, week, academics, clubs, scratchpad, and activity views.
impact_rationale: Students face real scheduling, course-selection, and continuity burdens; a combined planning and research workspace has credible value.
impact_evidence: Specific freshman-year Stanford planning audience.
Course sections, work-study, clubs, and rehearsals are integrated into planning.
creativity_rationale: The synthesis of academic planning, catalog research, and agent-human provenance is fresh, though the underlying category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent and student co-author plans with visible provenance.
usability_note: Integrated views and edit provenance are useful; Stanford-specific scope limits portability.
red_flags: demo_alive is unknown; packet evidence is primarily packaging and video.
standouts: Strong information architecture for a specific student workflow.
advance_reason: Complete-looking, high-value student workflow with strong structured-state rationale.

one_line: Private local-first fitness planner that turns intentions into a livable week.
what_it_does: Plans and guides workouts, tracks habits and progress, suggests schedule changes, and offers practical meal discovery.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the coach live plan state and lets it propose bounded schedule changes, but much of the outcome remains possible through ordinary app interaction.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly identifies coach suggestions via WebMCP.
Planner preserves existing workouts while adding proposals.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a substantial coherent product with dashboard, planner, guided workout, meals, settings, and progress surfaces; frame sheets show product motion.
execution_evidence: Three video frame sheets and eleven gallery images.
Explicit guided workout and planning workflows.
impact_rationale: People starting or returning to exercise have a clear adherence problem, and realistic scheduling plus one next action directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Specific audience and intention-to-action framing.
Progress, recovery, habits, and schedule adaptation are connected.
creativity_rationale: A thoughtful synthesis and privacy posture in a familiar fitness-planning category, with a moderate new angle rather than a novel concept.
creativity_evidence: Coach proposes changes without overwriting the user's plan.
usability_note: One-next-action framing and explicit finish control are promising; breadth may increase setup burden.
red_flags: Health guidance needs careful boundaries beyond a hackathon prototype.
standouts: Respectful coach model that preserves user ownership.
advance_reason: Strong execution and audience fit, with meaningful though not transformative leverage.

one_line: Protocol layer for discoverable, risk-aware, receipted WebMCP actions.
what_it_does: Adds page description, structured receipts, risk labels, human handoff tokens, and readiness gating to WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: This directly changes agent reliability and safety at the protocol boundary; the structured surface is the product and is difficult to replicate comparably with UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Five protocol capabilities are specified: describe_page, receipts, risk, request_human, and ready gating.
Five-step before/after Grant Portal demo is described.
execution_rationale: The concept is tightly scoped, technically coherent, open source, and framed with a concrete integration/demo; frame sheets support the live demo story.
execution_evidence: Public MIT repository and alive demo.
Three video sheets for the Grant Portal comparison.
Description states three-line integration and structured failure fields.
impact_rationale: Any site exposing agent actions can benefit from clearer discovery, risk boundaries, receipts, and human handoff, especially for consequential workflows.
impact_evidence: Addresses recurring agent failures: guessing controls, vague validation, async readiness, irreversible actions.
General site-owner integration target.
creativity_rationale: A memorable, practical extension of WebMCP that treats pages as responsible communicators rather than passive tool surfaces.
creativity_evidence: Single-use scoped human handoff and readiness gating are distinctive protocol primitives.
usability_note: Low integration burden is compelling; protocol adoption and interoperability remain open questions.
standouts: Strongest direct protocol contribution in this packet.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage, strong technical execution, and broad credible utility.

one_line: Agent-driven collaborative SVG logo editor with a large icon library.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect and edit layers, search icons, apply brand presets, restore share codes, and compose logos on the same canvas as a human.
leverage_rationale: Structured layer IDs, partial updates, icon search, and shared canvas state improve precision over UI clicking, but a capable general agent could achieve much of the same outcome with effort.
leverage_evidence: Six named tools cover state, layers, icons, presets, and share restoration.
Description emphasizes same live canvas for human and agent.
execution_rationale: A real editor, extensive library, brand presets, and multiple state-management operations indicate a complete scoped product; frame sheets clearly show the editor and finished preview.
execution_evidence: Three product-motion sheets show an open logo editor with canvas and controls.
Public repository and alive demo.
Description specifies partial and full-state workflows.
impact_rationale: Small teams and non-designers have a real need for fast logo iteration; shared agent composition can reduce mechanical design work.
impact_evidence: Free no-signup editor and 333k+ icon library.
Concrete brand-preset and PNG-to-SVG use cases.
creativity_rationale: Human-agent co-editing of a live vector canvas is a fresh interaction, though logo generation itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent manipulates semantic layers rather than only generating an image.
usability_note: No-signup and share codes help; quality depends heavily on prompt specificity and design judgment.
red_flags: Frame sheets do not clearly show an agent call; logo text is small.
standouts: Good semantic tool surface for an inherently visual editor.
advance_reason: Solid execution and useful shared-canvas leverage, despite familiar category.

one_line: Signed, scoped, receipt-producing security layer for agent messages and capabilities.
what_it_does: Attaches signatures, parent-grant capability tokens, chained receipt hashes, verification, and tamper detection to agent interactions.
leverage_rationale: Identity, authorization scope, and tamper-evident receipts address trust properties that ordinary UI automation cannot provide.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies signatures, parent grants, scoped capabilities, and chained receipts.
Demo includes Verify Intact and Verify Broken states.
execution_rationale: The security model is coherent and the packet describes both normal and tampered verification flows, with public code and video evidence.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show the Hub/Compare/Verify workflow.
Public repository and named verification states.
Description explains low-installation integration.
impact_rationale: Provenance and authorization are real infrastructure needs as agents gain access to sensitive actions and data.
impact_evidence: Targets proof of sender, destination, and allowed capability.
Tamper verification is directly relevant to auditability.
creativity_rationale: The signature/scope/receipt framing is an original extension of WebMCP into verifiable agent communication, pursued with a memorable visual protocol identity.
creativity_evidence: Continuous receipt hash chain and parent-grant model.
Security protocol surfaced through interactive verification.
usability_note: Minimal installation is promising, but key management and ecosystem adoption could be difficult.
red_flags: Protocol claims are demonstrated mainly through a focused demo rather than deployment evidence.
standouts: Strong trust and provenance angle beyond basic tool registration.
advance_reason: High leverage and distinctive security model with credible implementation evidence.

one_line: No-login file requests routed into Drive with agent-queryable submission tracking.
what_it_does: Creates public upload links, sorts and renames files into Google Drive, records a Sheets ledger, and answers status questions through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: The agent can create structured collection workflows and query live submission state precisely, spanning setup and follow-up tasks that are cumbersome through generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Four tools cover link creation, listing, submission search, and activation.
Description connects creation with questions such as whether Acme submitted.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent business workflow from public intake through Drive/Sheets recording and status lookup; video sheets show the product flow.
execution_evidence: Three video sheets and alive demo link.
Detailed field, folder, naming, deadline, PIN, and extension behavior.
impact_rationale: Small businesses routinely collect files from external parties and manually reconcile them; this directly removes that recurring administrative burden.
impact_evidence: Specific subcontractor invoice and onboarding-document audience.
Drive and Sheets outputs fit existing workflows.
creativity_rationale: A practical and well-chosen synthesis of anonymous intake and conversational operations, with moderate novelty.
creativity_evidence: Agent handles both before-the-link setup and after-the-upload reconciliation.
usability_note: No-account submitters and familiar Google destinations are strong; owner authentication and configuration remain friction points.
red_flags: Claims of live payments are unverified by the packet; Google integration dependency.
standouts: Clear end-to-end operational workflow with a useful conversational follow-up.
advance_reason: Strong real-world business value and substantial structured-state delta.

one_line: Specification-aware bill-of-materials commerce for construction products.
what_it_does: Helps agents map building specifications and code requirements to exact products, quantities, and purchasable BOMs.
leverage_rationale: Structured product/specification matching and transaction-ready BOM state can materially reduce hallucination and manual comparison versus an agent browsing product pages.
leverage_evidence: Pitch targets conversion of specs into BOM transactions.
Frame storyboard shows product-detail states and text/output overlays.
execution_rationale: The problem and initial fire-life-safety scope are coherent, but the packet does not clearly show a completed BOM or transaction end state.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show a fire-extinguisher ecommerce flow.
Description defines specifications, codes, quantities, and quote/order goals.
impact_rationale: Construction procurement has high-cost manual specification work and safety/compliance consequences; even a narrow fire-products workflow has credible niche value.
impact_evidence: Concrete building-code and fire-life-safety use case.
Description identifies manual multi-party comparison and quantity work.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to translate complex construction specifications into purchasable BOMs is an ambitious and less common commerce interaction.
creativity_evidence: Specification-to-transaction bridge rather than generic product search.
usability_note: Potentially powerful for specialists, but requirements interpretation and review burden are high.
red_flags: No clearly visible final BOM, quote, or checkout completion in frame evidence.
standouts: Ambitious vertical workflow with real high-friction domain work.
advance_reason: High-value, original vertical application; execution evidence is incomplete but sufficient for advancement.

one_line: Open scientific-figure editor with semantic agent composition and provenance.
what_it_does: Lets researchers assemble biological and lab-workflow figures using open assets, semantic commands, layout, connectors, annotations, validation, and export.
leverage_rationale: Semantic scene inspection, asset provenance, composition, geometry-aware connectors, validation, and export are a major improvement over coordinate-level UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Description lists stable IDs, bounded schemas, structured errors, and high-level scientific commands.
Agent and researcher edit through the same transaction system.
execution_rationale: The described command layer and export scope are substantial, but the frame sheets show small/partially legible diagrams and do not clearly prove a polished end-to-end figure workflow.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show evolving scientific-diagram-like canvas states.
Description specifies editing, layout, connectors, annotations, validation, and export.
impact_rationale: Researchers and educators have a real need for efficient, affordable scientific figure creation; open assets and publication exports make the fit credible.
impact_evidence: Specific biological reactions and lab-workflow audience.
Open-source alternative to paid scientific figure editors.
creativity_rationale: The semantic abstraction of scientific stages, interactions, geometry, and provenance is a notably original agent-editor interaction.
creativity_evidence: Moves beyond low-level move/resize commands to domain concepts.
Asset provenance is built into composition.
usability_note: Semantic commands can reduce layout burden; the sparse/partly legible frame evidence leaves polish and learnability uncertain.
red_flags: Frame sheets contain sparse and difficult-to-read canvas states; end-to-end export is not visibly demonstrated.
standouts: Strong domain-specific semantic command design and provenance emphasis.
advance_reason: Original high-leverage scientific editing workflow with credible audience value, tempered by thin visual proof.
